headings: Our Off-the-shelf, Multiplexed-engineered, iPSC-derived Cellular Immunotherapy Pipeline
Intellectual Property Relating to iPSC Technology and Platform
paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to bringing a transformative pipeline of off-the-shelf cellular immunotherapies to patients.

We have pioneered a therapeutic approach that we generally refer to as cellular programming: we create and engineer human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) to incorporate novel synthetic controls of cell function; after the engineering step that incorporates multiple functional elements into the iPSCs, we generate a clonal master iPSC line for use as a renewable source of starting material for the manufacture of cell therapies; through the manufacturing process, we direct the fate of the clonal master iPSC line to produce our cell therapy product candidates that are uniform in composition. Analogous to master cell lines used to manufacture biopharmaceutical drug products such as monoclonal antibodies, we believe our proprietary clonal master iPSC lines can be used to mass produce multiplexed-engineered, cellular immunotherapies which have off-the-shelf and on-demand availability, and that can be administered alone or in combination with standard-of-care therapies, to make cell therapies accessible to all.

Utilizing our iPSC product platform, we are developing off-the-shelf, multiplexed-engineered T-cell and natural killer (NK) cell product candidates which are selectively designed and incorporate novel synthetic controls of cell function to uniquely enhance the therapeutic capacity of the drug product to deliver multiple therapeutic mechanisms to patients. We have a pipeline of iPSC-derived, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-targeted T-cell and NK cell product candidates currently under development:

The use of human cells as therapeutic entities has disease-transforming potential across a broad spectrum of severe, life-threatening diseases. One particular form of cell therapy, CAR T-cell therapy, has emerged as a revolutionary and potentially curative treatment for patients with certain hematologic malignancies. In fact, multiple CAR T-cell therapies have now been approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for a number of disease indications, including relapsed / refractory B-cell malignancies and relapsed / refractory multiple myeloma. Additionally, several groups have demonstrated use of CAR T-cell therapy for the treatment of autoimmune diseases including systemic lupus erythematosus, idiopathic inflammatory myositis, systemic sclerosis, and myasthenia gravis.

Cell therapies approved for commercialization, as well as those undergoing clinical development, today most often rely on the use of autologous, or a patient's own, cells and are generally only available for patient treatment at a limited number of specialized medical centers. Sourcing, engineering, expanding and delivering cells patient-by-patient is logistically complex and expensive, resource intensive, and challenging to manufacture as the drug product is often heterogeneous in consistency with batch-to-batch variability. Furthermore, the widespread use of viral vectors to deliver genetic information into the patient's T cells continues to raise long-term safety concerns. Significant hurdles remain to ensure that autologous cell therapies can be consistently manufactured and reliably delivered at the scale necessary to support broad patient access. While donor-derived allogeneic cell therapies offer some solutions, challenges remain with respect to uniformity of the engineered drug product, limited ability to incorporate multiple functions through engineering, reduced capabilities to scale the manufacture process, and donor-to-donor variability.

We believe iPSCs, which possess the unique dual properties of unlimited self-renewal and differentiation potential into all cell types of the body, can be used to overcome key limitations inherent to the manufacture, development and commercialization of today's cell therapies. We have established a proprietary iPSC product platform and have amassed significant internal expertise in the production of off-the-shelf, multiplexed-engineered, T-cell and NK cell product candidates for therapeutic use. Our proprietary iPSC product platform includes: generating, engineering, isolating and characterizing single-cell iPSC clones; creating, qualifying, and cryopreserving clonal master iPSC lines; differentiating clonal master cell iPSC lines to produce T cells and NK cells at scale; and cryopreserving and storing these T cells and NK cells under conditions that support multi-year stability. Our cell product candidates can be mass-produced at significant scale in a cost-effective manner, are well-defined and uniform in composition, and can be stored in inventory and delivered off-the-shelf to maximize patient reach and accessibility. Our proprietary iPSC product platform is supported by an intellectual property portfolio of over 600 issued patents and 550 pending patent applications.

We operate a 40,000+ square foot fully integrated Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) facility for manufacturing of our iPSC-derived CAR T-cell and CAR NK cell product candidates that is intended to support all phases of clinical development as well as initial commercialization. We believe our therapeutic approach is highly differentiated and has the potential to overcome numerous challenges associated with today's cell therapies, address significant unmet need, and broadly deliver transformative medical benefits for patients.
Our mission is to bring off-the-shelf cellular immunotherapies with disease-transforming potential initially to patients with autoimmune diseases and cancer. The key pillars of our strategy include:

• Establish therapeutic differentiation with FT819 for the treatment of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with and without lupus nephritis. Autoimmune diseases affect organs throughout the body and are often characterized by the presence of auto-antibodies, which are produced by aberrant B cells and can attack healthy cells and tissues. The chronic and debilitating nature of these diseases results in substantial medical expenses and a low quality of life, creating a significant burden for patients, their families and the health care system. Current treatment options for SLE, with or without lupus nephritis, include corticosteroids, immunosuppressive medications, and biologics; however, these treatments often require long-term use, are associated with life-threatening side effects, and fail to provide adequate disease control.

We believe FT819, our off-the-shelf, iPSC-derived, CD19-targeted CAR T-cell product candidate, designed to balance safety and efficacy, has the potential to eliminate disease-causing B cells, enable reconstitution of a healthy immune cell compartment, and induce complete and durable responses in B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases. This approach is supported by a ground-breaking academic clinical study published in Nature Medicine in September 2022, in which patients with SLE received intensive conditioning chemotherapy, consisting of multi-day dosing of cyclophosphamide (Cy) and fludarabine (Flu), followed by an investigational autologous CD19-targeted CAR T-cell therapy. The treatment induced rapid B-cell depletion and elimination of auto-antibody production, leading to clinical remission. Recovery of a naïve B-cell compartment occurred several months after treatment, enabling an "immune rebalance" without signs of humoral autoimmunity for the first five patients.

We are currently conducting a multi-center, Phase 1 clinical trial of FT819 for the treatment of moderate-to-severe SLE, with treatment sites in the United States, United Kingdom (U.K.), and European Union (EU). In contrast to treatment with autologous CAR T-cell therapy, patients enrolled in our Phase 1 clinical study are not required to undergo apheresis, are treated with a less intense flu-free conditioning regimen and receive FT819 on-demand without discontinuing their current treatment, which increases patient accessibility and reach. In addition, our Phase 1 clinical trial includes the opportunity for patients to receive FT819 as an add-on to current maintenance therapy in the absence of conditioning chemotherapy, an approach that combines the potency of a CAR T cell with the availability and accessibility of traditional medicine.

In April 2025, we were granted regenerative medicine advanced therapy (RMAT) designation by the FDA for FT819 to treat moderate-to-severe SLE. The RMAT designation was established under the 21st Century Cures Act to expedite the

development and review of regenerative medicine therapies for serious or life-threatening diseases or conditions. Our RMAT application included initial clinical safety and activity data from patients treated with FT819 in its ongoing multi-center, Phase 1 clinical trial. We plan to pursue differentiated treatment approaches, including treatment of patients in community settings without hospitalization, and novel registrational strategies with the FDA under its RMAT designation. We received authorization from the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) in August 2025 and from the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in October 2025 to initiate clinical trials of FT819 in the U.K. and EU, respectively. We plan to continue to expand our clinical investigation outside of the United States in 2026. We believe our therapeutic approach with FT819 and its accessibility is highly differentiated and may offer a more convenient and favorable experience for patients, including outpatient treatment. We intend to continue the regulatory development of FT819 in SLE, with the submission of a Phase 2 registration-enabling clinical protocol in lupus nephritis and subsequently investigate the potential of FT819 as a treatment for extrarenal lupus in a second trial, with the ultimate goal to advance to biologics license application (BLA) filing over the course of the next several years.

• Expand the clinical footprint of our iPSC product platform within the field of autoimmunity, including initiating clinical investigations in additional B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases. The prevalence of autoimmune diseases is both widespread and growing, with over 80 known autoimmune diseases affecting up to 8% of the U.S. population. Since the targeting and deep depletion of B cells may be a key mechanism of action to enable an immune rebalance and durable clinical responses across autoimmune diseases, we plan to expand our clinical investigation of FT819 within the field of autoimmunity. In December 2024, we reached agreement with the FDA to allow for the clinical investigation of additional B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases under our current Phase 1 clinical trial of FT819. In February 2025, we amended our clinical protocol to include three additional diseases: anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV), idiopathic inflammatory myositis (IIM), and systemic sclerosis (SSc). With completion of the dose-escalation cohort for the second dose level (900 million cells) in SLE, we have initiated dose-expansion cohorts in SSc, AAV and IIM. In October 2025, we treated our first SSc patient and are pursuing the treatment of additional patients. We believe the independent assessment of multiple B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases under one Phase 1 basket study enables the most cost-effective and efficient pathway for broad clinical development.

headings: Risks Related to the Discovery, Development and Regulation of Our Product Candidates
If we fail to complete the preclinical or clinical development of, or to obtain regulatory approval for, our product candidates, our business would be significantly harmed.
We may face delays in initiating, conducting or completing our clinical trials, and we may not be able to initiate, conduct or complete them at all.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors, as well as the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, and in our other public filings. The occurrence of any of these risks could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or growth prospects or cause our actual results to differ materially from those contained in forward-looking statements we have made in this report and those we may make from time to time. You should consider all of the risk factors described in our public filings when evaluating our business.

All of our product candidates are currently in research or early clinical development. We have not completed clinical development of or obtained regulatory approval for any of our product candidates. Only a small percentage of research and development programs ultimately result in commercially successful products, and we cannot assure you that any of our product candidates will demonstrate the safety, purity and potency, or efficacy profiles necessary to support further preclinical study, clinical development or regulatory approval. In addition, we have historically focused on the development of cell therapies for cancer. We have limited prior experience in developing treatments for autoimmune diseases, and there are no cell therapies approved in the United States to treat autoimmune diseases.

We may experience delays in, or pause or cancel our ongoing and planned clinical development activities or research and development activities for any of our product candidates for a variety of reasons, including:

• difficulties in optimizing the right dose and dosing schedule for our product candidates, which might result in a determination that a product candidate is ineffective, causes harmful side effects, or otherwise presents unacceptable safety risks during clinical trials or has an unfavorable toxicity profile in preclinical studies or early clinical trials to support initiating or continuing clinical investigation;

• difficulties in manufacturing or distributing a product candidate, including the inability to manufacture and distribute a product candidate in a sufficient quantity, suitable form, or in a cost-effective manner, or under protocols and processes and with materials and facilities acceptable to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or comparable foreign regulatory authorities for the conduct of clinical trials or for marketing approval;

• challenges in making arrangements with various medical divisions across hospitals or with other treatment centers for administration of our product candidates, including with treatment centers and relevant hospital divisions to perform infusion of our product candidates;

In addition, we have entered into research collaborations and license agreements with academic institutions to support the development of our iPSC product platform and our off-the-shelf product candidates.

We have also entered into collaborations with pharmaceutical companies to research, develop and commercialize off-the-shelf, multiplexed-engineered, iPSC-derived CAR T-cell and CAR NK cell product candidates for the treatment of cancer. In September 2018, we entered into a collaboration and option agreement (Ono Agreement) with Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Ono), under which we are currently researching and developing iPSC-derived CAR T-cell and CAR NK cell product candidates for the treatment of solid tumors.

We were incorporated in Delaware in 2007 and are headquartered in San Diego, California. Since our inception in 2007, we have devoted substantially all of our resources to our cell programming approach and the research and development of our product candidates, the creation, licensing and protection of related intellectual property, and the provision of general and administrative support for these activities. To date, we have funded our operations primarily through the public and private sale of common stock and warrants, the private placement of preferred stock and convertible notes, commercial bank debt and revenues from collaboration activities and grants.

We have never been profitable and have incurred net losses in each year since inception. Substantially all of our net losses resulted from costs incurred in connection with our research and development programs and from general and administrative costs associated with our operations. We expect to continue to incur operating losses for at least the foreseeable future. Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and year to year. We expect our expenses will remain significant in connection with our ongoing and planned activities as we:

headings: 本公司現成、多重工程設計、iPSC 來源細胞免疫治療產品線

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段的生技藥品公司，致力於為患者提供具變革性的現成細胞免疫療法產品管線。

我們已開創一種治療方式，我們通常稱之為細胞程式設計：我們創造並工程化人類誘導多功能幹細胞（iPSCs），以整合新型合成控制元件以控制細胞功能；在工程化步驟中，我們將多種功能性元件整合至iPSCs中，以產生一個克隆主iPSC線，作為製造細胞療法的可持續來源起始材料；透過製造過程，我們能導向克隆主iPSC線的命運，以製造出組成均一的細胞療法產品候選品。類似於製造生物製藥藥品（如單克隆抗體）所使用的主細胞線，我們相信我們的專利克隆主iPSC線可用於大規模生產多重工程化的細胞免疫療法產品，具有現成且即時可用的特性，並可單獨或與標準療法組合使用，以使細胞療法更易於普及。
利用我們的iPSC產品平台，我們正在開發現成、多重工程化的T細胞與自然殺傷（NK）細胞產品候選品，這些產品經過選擇性設計，並整合新型合成控制元件以獨特增強藥品的治療能力，以提供多種治療機制給患者。我們目前正在開發的iPSC衍生、嵌合抗原受體（CAR）目標T細胞與NK細胞產品候選品包括：

使用人類細胞作為治療載體，對廣泛的嚴重、威脅生命的疾病具有改變疾病的潛力。其中一種細胞療法，即CAR T細胞療法，已成為治療某些血液惡性腫瘤患者的革命性且可能具有根治性的治療方式。事實上，多種CAR T細胞療法已獲得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准，用於治療多種疾病，包括復發/難治性B細胞惡性腫瘤及復發/難治性多發性骨髓瘤。此外，多個研究團隊已展示CAR T細胞療法在治療自身免疫疾病（如系統性紅斑狼瘡、原發性炎症性肌炎、系統性硬化症及重症肌無力）的應用。

目前已核准商業化或正在進行臨牀開發的細胞療法，大多數依賴使用自體細胞（即患者的自身細胞），且通常只能在少數專門醫療中心提供患者治療。從來源、工程化、擴增及交付細胞的過程，對每位患者而言，皆具備複雜且昂貴的物流與資源需求，且製造過程困難，因藥品常因批次不同而一致性差異大。此外，廣泛使用病毒載體將遺傳資訊送入患者的T細胞，持續引發長期安全性疑慮。要確保自體細胞療法能穩定製造並可靠交付，以支持廣泛患者使用，仍面臨重大挑戰。雖然捐贈衍生的異體細胞療法提供了一些解決方案，但仍有關於工程化藥品一致性、有限的工程化多重功能整合能力、製造過程擴充能力不足，以及捐贈者之間的變異性等挑戰。

我們相信iPSCs具有獨特的雙重特性：無限自我更新與分化為體內所有細胞類型的潛力，可用以克服現有細胞療法在製造、開發與商業化方面的關鍵限制。我們已建立專利的iPSC產品平台，並累積了大量內部專業知識，用以生產現成、多重工程化的T細胞與NK細胞產品候選品，以供治療用途。我們的專利iPSC產品平台包括：產生、工程化、分離與鑑定單細胞iPSC克隆；建立、驗證與冷凍保存克隆主iPSC線；將克隆主iPSC線分化為大規模生產T細胞與NK細胞；以及在支持多達數年穩定性的條件下冷凍保存與儲存這些T細胞與NK細胞。我們的細胞產品候選品可以高規模、低成本的方式大量生產，具有明確且組成均一的特性，並可儲存於存貨中，以現成方式交付，以最大化患者接觸與可近性。我們的專利iPSC產品平台受到超過600項已發明專利與550項待審專利申請的智慧財產權組合支持。
我們運營一個40,000平方英尺以上的完整整合式良好製造實踐（GMP）製造廠，用於製造我們的iPSC衍生CAR T細胞與CAR NK細胞產品候選品，旨在支持所有臨牀開發階段以及初步商業化。我們相信我們的治療方式具有高度差異性，並有潛力克服現有細胞療法的許多挑戰，解決重大未滿足的醫療需求，並廣泛提供變革性的醫療效益給患者。
我們的使命是將具疾病變革潛力的現成細胞免疫療法，首先提供給患有自身免疫疾病與癌症的患者。我們策略的關鍵支柱包括：

• 建立 FT819 與治療全身性紅斑狼瘡 (SLE) 的療效差異，包括有與無狼瘡腎炎的情況。自身免疫疾病會影響身體各器官，且常以產生自體抗體為特徵，這些抗體由異常 B 細胞產生，可能攻擊健康細胞與組織。這些疾病的慢性與使人衰弱的特性，導致顯著的醫療費用與低品質生活，對患者、其家屬與醫療系統造成重大負擔。目前治療 SLE 的選項，包括有或無狼瘡腎炎，包含類固醇、免疫抑制藥物與生物製劑；然而，這些治療常需長期使用，與致命性副作用相關，且無法提供足夠的疾病控制。

我們認為 FT819，我們的現成製備、iPSC 來源、CD19 導向的 CAR T 細胞產品候選藥物，設計上平衡安全性與療效，有潛力消除致病 B 細胞，恢復健康的免疫細胞組成，並在 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病中引發完全且持續的反應。這種方法受到 2022 年 9 月發表於 Nature Medicine 的突破性學術臨牀研究支持，該研究中 SLE 患者接受強效的條件化化療，包含多日劑量的環磷醯胺 (Cy) 與氟達拉濱 (Flu)，隨後接受實驗性的自體 CD19 導向 CAR T 細胞治療。治療引發快速 B 細胞減少與自體抗體產生的消除，導致臨牀緩解。治療後數個月恢復 naïve B 細胞組成，使「免疫再平衡」發生，前五位患者未出現體液型自身免疫症狀。

我們目前正在美國、英國 (U.K.) 與歐盟 (EU) 多中心進行 FT819 的 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，用於治療中度至重度 SLE。與自體 CAR T 細胞治療不同，參與我們 Phase 1 臨牀試驗的患者無需進行血液分離，接受較不強烈的無氟條件化化療方案，並可按需接受 FT819 治療，而不需中斷現有治療，這提高了患者的可近性與可達性。此外，我們的 Phase 1 臨牀試驗包含患者在無條件化化療的情況下，將 FT819 作為現有維持治療的附加治療，這種方法結合 CAR T 細胞的強效與傳統藥物的可近性與可達性。
2025 年 4 月，我們獲得美國食品藥物管理局 (FDA) 授予 FT819 的再生醫學先進療法 (RMAT) 認定，用於治療中度至重度 SLE。RMAT 認定根據 21 世紀治癒法案 (21st Century Cures Act) 設立，以加速

再生醫學療法的開發與審評，用於嚴重或致命性疾病或病症。我們的 RMAT 申請包含來自 FT819 在進行中的多中心、Phase 1 臨牀試驗中接受治療患者的初始臨牀安全性與活性數據。我們計畫追求差異化的治療方法，包括在社區設施中治療患者而無需住院，並與 FDA 在其 RMAT 認定下採用創新註冊策略。我們在 2025 年 8 月獲得英國藥物與醫療產品管理局 (MHRA) 的授權，並在 2025 年 10 月獲得歐洲藥物管理局 (EMA) 的授權，分別開始在英國與 EU 進行 FT819 的臨牀試驗。我們計畫在 2026 年繼續擴展在美國以外的臨牀研究。我們認為 FT819 的治療方法與其可近性具有高度差異化，可能為患者提供更方便且有利的體驗，包括門診治療。我們計畫繼續在 SLE 中進行 FT819 的監管開發，並在狼瘡腎炎中提交 Phase 2 登記啟動臨牀協議，隨後在第二個試驗中探討 FT819 作為治療非腎臟狼瘡的潛力，最終目標是在未來數年內提交生物製劑許可申請 (BLA)。

• 擴展我們 iPSC 產品平台在自身免疫疾病領域的臨牀應用範圍，包括在其他 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病中啟動臨牀研究。自身免疫疾病的盛行率既廣泛又持續增加，已知的自身免疫疾病超過 80 種，影響美國人口高達 8%。由於針對並深度清除 B 細胞可能是實現免疫再平衡及持久臨牀反應的關鍵機制，我們計畫擴展 FT819 在自身免疫疾病領域的臨牀研究。2024 年 12 月，我們與美國食品藥物管理局達成協議，允許在目前 FT819 第一期臨牀試驗的框架下，對其他 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病進行臨牀研究。2025 年 2 月，我們修訂臨牀試驗計畫，新增三種疾病：抗中性粒細胞胞質抗體相關血管炎（AAV）、原發性發炎性肌症（IIM）及系統性硬化症（SSc）。隨著在系統性紅斑狼瘡（SLE）中第二劑量層級（900 百萬細胞）的劑量遞增組完成，我們已啟動在 SSc、AAV 和 IIM 中的劑量擴展組。2025 年 10 月，我們治療了首位 SSc 患者，並正在追蹤治療其他患者。我們認為在一期臨牀試驗中對多種 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病進行獨立評估，能提供最有效率且成本效益最高的廣泛臨牀發展途徑。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之分析，並與我們合併財務報表及相關附註（包含於本年度報告表 10-K 的第 8 項項目）一併參考。下列討論包含風險與不確定性之向前看陳述。我們實際結果可能與任何向前看陳述所表達或暗示者有重大差異，原因可能為多種因素，包括於「項目 1A. 風險因素」標題下所列者。
我們是一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，致力於為患者帶來具變革性的現成細胞免疫療法產品線。

我們已開創一種治療方法，我們通常稱為細胞程式化（cellular programming）：我們創造並工程化人類誘導多功能幹細胞（iPSCs），使其 incorporates 新型合成控制以控制細胞功能；在工程化步驟中，我們將多種功能元件整合至 iPSCs 中，並產生一個克隆主 iPSC 系列，用作製造細胞療法之可持續來源的起始材料；透過製造過程，我們可導向克隆主 iPSC 系列的命運，以製造我們的細胞療法產品候選品，使其組成均勻。類似於製造生物藥品（如單克隆抗體）所使用的主細胞線，我們相信我們的專利克隆主 iPSC 系列可用於大量生產多重工程化細胞免疫療法產品，這些產品具有現成可用性與按需可用性，並可單獨使用或與標準療法結合使用，以使細胞療法對所有患者皆可取得。

利用我們的 iPSC 產品平台，我們正在開發現成可用、多重工程化 T 細胞與自然殺傷（NK）細胞產品候選品，這些產品經過選擇性設計，並 incorporates 新型合成控制以控制細胞功能，以獨特提升藥品的治療能力，為患者提供多重治療機制。我們目前正在開發 iPSC 來源、嵌合抗原受體（CAR）目標 T 細胞與 NK 細胞產品候選品。此外，我們已與學術機構簽訂研究合作與授權協議，以支持我們的 iPSC 產品平台及現成產品候選品的開發。
我們也與藥品公司簽訂合作協議，以研究、開發與商業化現成可用、多重工程化、iPSC 來源的 CAR T 細胞與 CAR NK 細胞產品候選品，用以治療癌症。2018 年 9 月，我們與 Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.（Ono）簽訂合作與選擇權協議（Ono 協議），目前我們正在研究與開發 iPSC 來源的 CAR T 細胞與 CAR NK 細胞產品候選品，用以治療實體腫瘤。
我們於 2007 年在特拉華州註冊成立，總部設於美國加利福尼亞州聖地牙哥市。自 2007 年成立以來，我們已將幾乎所有資源投入我們的細胞程式化方法，以及我們產品候選品的研究與開發、相關智慧財產權的創造、授權與保護，以及這些活動的總務與行政支援。截至目前為止，我們主要透過公開與私下發行普通股與認購權證、私下發行優先股與可轉換票據、商業銀行貸款及合作活動與補助金所產生的收入來資助運作。
我們從未獲利，且自成立以來每年均產生淨虧損。我們的淨虧損幾乎全部來自與我們研究與開發計畫相關的費用，以及與我們運作相關的總務與行政費用。我們預期至少在可預見的未來，仍將持續產生營運虧損。我們的淨虧損可能在季度與年度之間有顯著波動。我們預期與我們持續進行及計畫進行的活動相關的費用將持續保持在高水平，我們：
• 進行我們持續進行及計畫進行的產品候選品之前期臨牀研究與臨牀試驗，這可能包括與臨牀研究機構（CROs）簽訂協議所產生的更高臨牀試驗費用，包括在美國境外進行的試驗。
• 進行良好製造規範 (GMP) 生產，包括透過委外製造機構 (CMOs) 進行部分或全部製造我們 iPSC 來源細胞產品候選品、製程與擴大量產開發及技術轉移活動，以製造我們的產品候選品，包括正在進行臨牀試驗及 Investigational New Drug (IND) 申請所需的前期臨牀開發活動；
• 購置用以製造我們產品候選品的實驗室設備、材料及用品，以支持我們的臨牀試驗及研究活動的進行；
• 繼續我們的研究、開發與製造活動，包括根據我們與 Ono 簽訂的贊助研究及合作協議；
• 維護、聲請、保護、擴充及執行我們的智慧財產權組合；
• 與監管當局合作進行產品候選品的開發，並尋求相關監管核准；
• 繼續在本公司總部進行業務運作，包括維持內部 GMP 生產能力；

headings: 與本公司產品候選藥物之發現、開發及規範相關之風險
若本公司未能完成產品候選藥物之臨牀前或臨牀開發，或未能取得相關規範審批，將對本公司業務造成重大損害。
本公司可能面臨延誤啟動、進行或完成臨牀試驗之情形，且可能無法啟動、進行或完成任何臨牀試驗。
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考量下列風險因素，以及本年度報告表 10-K 中的其他資訊，以及我們其他公開申報文件。上述任何風險事件的發生，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及/或成長前景造成損害，或導致我們實際結果與本報告中所作的預測性陳述，或我們未來不時所作的預測性陳述有重大差異。評估我們業務時，您應考量我們公開申報文件中所描述的所有風險因素。

我們所有產品候選品目前均處於研究或早期臨牀開發階段。我們尚未完成任何產品候選品的臨牀開發，也未取得任何產品候選品的監管批准。僅有少數研究與開發計畫最終會發展為商業成功的產品，我們無法保證任何產品候選品能顯示出足夠的安全性、純度與效力，或有效性資料，以支持進一步的非臨牀研究、臨牀開發或監管批准。此外，我們歷來主要專注於癌症的細胞治療開發。我們在開發自身免疫疾病治療方案方面經驗有限，且美國目前尚無核准用於治療自身免疫疾病的細胞治療產品。
我們可能因多種原因而遭遇臨牀開發活動或研究與開發活動的延遲，或暫停或取消任何產品候選品的臨牀開發活動或研究與開發活動，包括：
• 難以優化產品候選品的正確劑量與給藥時程，這可能會導致判斷產品候選品無效、引起有害副作用，或在臨牀試驗中或其他非臨牀研究或早期臨牀試驗中，呈現不可接受的安全風險，或在支持進行或持續臨牀研究的過程中，具有不利的毒性資料；
• 難以製造或分發產品候選品，包括無法以足夠數量、合適形式或具成本效益的方式製造與分發產品候選品，或在符合美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）或相應外國監管機構所接受的協議與程序、材料與設施的條件下進行臨牀試驗或上市許可的製造與分發；
• 在醫院各醫療部門或其它治療中心安排產品候選品的施用時遇到困難，包括與治療中心及相關醫院部門協調進行產品候選品的靜脈注射。
